plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to zero.
This aligns with capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
Focus on broad index and income for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns. However, potential upside is also limited.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Trim QQQI to 25% to reduce income concentration.
Reduce all leveraged ETF positions (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to smaller allocations.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure to leveraged assets while reducing overall concentration.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by blending broad index, quality tech, and a small amount of leverage. It aims for risk-first growth, with moderate drawdowns and a balanced risk profile.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% and QQQI to 25% to meet mandates and rebalance.
Add to CRWD, pressing into a strong uptrending position.
Buy new positions in TECS, SQQQ, TZA, and SOXS, leveraging strong inverse setups.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to target higher growth, with strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leverage and high-scoring scanner setups. It carries significantly higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing exposure to income-generating ETFs.
Sell all leveraged and high-beta single names (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income, but distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff. This is not a savings account.
